It is EMPTY for the migrated mutants because their authors named no arm, and filling it from a later run would make the claim unfalsifiable. A mutant whose target has moved is RETIRED here, with the reason, rather than deleted -- `MUT REGISTRY-anchors-live` in the validator's selftest is what refuses to let it drift silently.

THIS LIST IS NOT MAINTAINED BY HAND ANY MORE -- `devflow-mutate.py --derived-census` applies two mutations that CANNOT change behaviour (a blank line above the subject's first statement, which moves every line number; and the operands of one commutative `or`, which moves bytes and no line numbers) and reports the arms they redden. Anything that reddens under a behaviour-free mutation is derived BY DEFINITION. The first hand-written version of this list named two arms and missed four, all in the `V30` family; the census found all four mechanically and the list is now its output. `ENC VERDICT-live` re-runs the WHOLE selftest in a child, so it reddens whenever anything else does -- and also when the child merely CRASHES, which no arm detected. `MUT REGISTRY-anchors-live` reads this registry against the STAGED tree, so a mutation that removes its own anchor reddens it BY CONSTRUCTION; it reports that a mutation happened, never that the subject broke.
